terms.gloss: be away, be absent; be … away (of distance)
evidence: Cic. Fam. 2.7.1: longē absum, audiō sērō (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 28: absēns, absentis, absent; also an absentee
terms.comment: The opposite of adsum. Of distance too: Quantum abest?, how far is it? (see how far).

evidence: Plaut. Capt. 1.2.5: sī forīs, sī intus volent (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The opposite of domī and intus; going out is forās. Away abroad is peregrē (see abroad).

terms.grammar: participle of absum, used as an adjective and a noun
terms.comment: “In my absence” is the ablative absolute mē absente.

phrases.latin: avē, mī Gāī, meus asellus jūcundissimus, quem semper medius fidius dēsīderō, cum ā mē abes
phrases.english: hello, my Gaius, my dearest little donkey, whom I always miss, I swear, when you’re away from me

sources: Lewis & Short: absum · Lewis & Short: foris
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-gellius, loci-cicero-epistulae), checked against the editions named there.
